name: Anti-Aliased Interlevel Loss
definition: A loss function for proposal supervision that measures the distance between a NeRF histogram (s, w) and a proposal histogram (ŝ, ŵ) by blurring the NeRF histogram into a piecewise-linear spline and resampling it into the proposal's interval endpoints to prevent aliasing.
summary: Anti-Aliased Interlevel Loss is a proposal supervision function that blurs NeRF histograms into piecewise-linear splines to prevent aliasing artifacts during training, unlike the piecewise constant loss in mip-NeRF 360.
